source.text: These JSON data structures MAY contain whitespace and/or line breaks before or after any JSON values or structural characters, in accordance with Section 2 of RFC 7159 [RFC7159].

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: In the JWE JSON Serialization, one or more of the JWE Protected Header, JWE Shared Unprotected Header, and JWE Per-Recipient Unprotected Header MUST be present.
The inclusion of some of these values is OPTIONAL.

notes: short REQUIRED/OPTIONAL usage; often a field-table label rather than a requirement

source.text: The Header Parameter names within the JOSE Header MUST be unique, just as described in Section 4 of [JWS].
This algorithm MUST be an AEAD algorithm with a specified key length.
This Header Parameter MUST be present and MUST be understood and processed by implementations.
Other values MAY be used.
When used, this Header Parameter MUST be integrity protected; therefore, it MUST occur only within the

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: Use of this Header Parameter is OPTIONAL.

notes: short REQUIRED/OPTIONAL usage; often a field-table label rather than a requirement

source.text: This Header Parameter MUST be understood and processed by implementations.
The CEK MUST have a length equal to that required for the content encryption algorithm.
However, in all cases, the encrypted content for at least one recipient MUST successfully validate or the JWE MUST be considered invalid.
When using the JWE JSON Serialization, this restriction includes that the same Header Parameter name also MUST NOT occur in distinct JSON object values that together comprise the JOSE Header.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: The CEK MUST have a length equal to that required for the content encryption algorithm.
If there was no recipient for which all of the decryption steps succeeded, then the JWE MUST be considered invalid.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: Even if a JWE can be successfully decrypted, unless the algorithms used in the JWE are acceptable to the application, it SHOULD consider the JWE to be invalid.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: protected The "protected" member MUST be present and contain the value BASE64URL(UTF8(JWE Protected Header)) when the JWE Protected Header value is non-empty; otherwise, it MUST be absent.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: unprotected The "unprotected" member MUST be present and contain the value JWE Shared Unprotected Header when the JWE Shared Unprotected Header value is non-empty; otherwise, it MUST be absent.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: iv The "iv" member MUST be present and contain the value BASE64URL(JWE Initialization Vector) when the JWE Initialization Vector value is non-empty; otherwise, it MUST be absent.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: aad The "aad" member MUST be present and contain the value BASE64URL(JWE AAD)) when the JWE AAD value is non-empty; otherwise, it MUST be absent.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: ciphertext The "ciphertext" member MUST be present and contain the value BASE64URL(JWE Ciphertext).
tag The "tag" member MUST be present and contain the value BASE64URL(JWE Authentication Tag) when the JWE Authentication Tag value is non-empty; otherwise, it MUST be absent.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: recipients The "recipients" member value MUST be an array of JSON objects.
This member MUST be present with exactly one array element per
header The "header" member MUST be present and contain the value JWE Per- Recipient Unprotected Header when the JWE Per-Recipient Unprotected Header value is non-empty; otherwise, it MUST be absent.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: encrypted_key The "encrypted_key" member MUST be present and contain the value BASE64URL(JWE Encrypted Key) when the JWE Encrypted Key value is non-empty; otherwise, it MUST be absent.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: At least one of the "header", "protected", and "unprotected" members MUST be present so that "alg" and "enc" Header Parameter values are conveyed for each recipient computation.
Additional members can be present in both the JSON objects defined above; if not understood by implementations encountering them, they MUST be ignored.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: The Header Parameter names in the three locations MUST be disjoint.
Therefore, all Header Parameters that specify the treatment of the plaintext value MUST be the same for all recipients.
This primarily means that the "enc" (encryption algorithm) Header Parameter value in the JOSE Header for each recipient and any parameters of that algorithm MUST be the same.
The "recipients" member MUST NOT be present when using this syntax.

notes: contains a conditional; capture the guard in `condition` rather than in `behavior`

source.text: To mitigate the attacks described in RFC 3218 [RFC3218], the recipient MUST NOT distinguish between format, padding, and length errors of encrypted keys.

lowercase_keyword_review.text: Note that some algorithms may not use an Initialization Vector, in which case this value is the empty octet sequence.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: As indicated by the common registry, JWSs and JWEs share a common Header Parameter space; when a parameter is used by both specifications, its usage must be compatible between the specifications.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: "enc" values should either be registered in the IANA "JSON Web Signature and Encryption Algorithms" registry established by [JWA] or be a value that contains a Collision-Resistant Name.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: However, in order to prevent collisions, any new Header Parameter name should either be registered in the IANA "JSON Web Signature and Encryption Header Parameters" registry established by [JWS] or be a Public Name: a value that contains a Collision-Resistant Name.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: New Header Parameters should be introduced sparingly, as they can result in non-interoperable JWEs.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: A producer and consumer of a JWE may agree to use Header Parameter names that are Private Names: names that are not Registered Header Parameter names (Section 4.1) or Public Header Parameter names (Section 4.2).
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: Unlike Public Header Parameter names, Private Header Parameter names are subject to collision and should be used with caution.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: Generate a random JWE Initialization Vector of the correct size for the content encryption algorithm (if required for the algorithm); otherwise, let the JWE Initialization Vector be the empty octet sequence.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: When there are multiple recipients, it is an application decision which of the recipients' encrypted content must successfully validate for the JWE to be accepted.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: In some cases, encrypted content for all recipients must successfully validate or the JWE will be considered invalid.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: Otherwise, when using the JWE JSON Serialization, let the JOSE Header be the union of the members of the JWE Protected Header, the JWE Shared Unprotected Header and the corresponding JWE Per-Recipient Unprotected Header, all of which must be completely valid JSON objects.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: Verify that the implementation understands and can process all fields that it is required to support, whether required by this specification, by the algorithms being used, or by the "crit" Header Parameter value, and that the values of those parameters are also understood and supported.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: Finally, note that it is an application decision which algorithms may be used in a given context.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: The Header Parameter values used when creating or validating per- recipient ciphertext and Authentication Tag values are the union of the three sets of Header Parameter values that may be present: (1) the JWE Protected Header represented in the "protected" member, (2) the JWE Shared Unprotected Header represented in the "unprotected" member, and (3) the JWE Per-Recipient Unprotected Header represented in the "header" member of the recipient's array element.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: All these methods will yield the same result for all legal input values; they may yield different results for malformed inputs.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: (Extracting the "alg" value to examine is straightforward when using the JWS Compact Serialization or the JWE Compact Serialization and may be more difficult when using the JWS JSON Serialization or the JWE JSON Serialization.)
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: All of the security issues that are pertinent to any cryptographic application must be addressed by JWS/JWE/JWK agents.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: In addition to the keys listed there that must be protected, implementations performing encryption must protect the key encryption key and the Content Encryption Key.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: Compromise of the key encryption key may result in the disclosure of all contents protected with that key.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: Similarly, compromise of the Content Encryption Key may result in disclosure of the associated encrypted content.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: Algorithms of matching strengths should be used together whenever possible.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: For instance, when AES Key Wrap is used with a given key size, using the same key size is recommended when AES GCM is also used.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: When decrypting, particular care must be taken not to allow the JWE recipient to be used as an oracle for decrypting messages.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: RFC 3218 [RFC3218] should be consulted for specific countermeasures to attacks on RSAES-PKCS1-v1_5.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: This means, for instance, that if the key is marked as being for "RSA-OAEP" only, any attempt to decrypt a message using the "RSA1_5" algorithm with that key should fail immediately due to invalid use of the key.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: It is strongly recommended, in the event of receiving an improperly formatted key, that the recipient substitute a randomly generated CEK and proceed to the next step, to mitigate timing attacks.
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords

lowercase_keyword_review.text: The plaintext, the CEK, JWE Initialization Vector, and JWE Protected Header are shared by all recipients (which must be the case, since the ciphertext and Authentication Tag are also shared).
lowercase_keyword_review.note: lowercase per RFC 8174: not normative by itself, but review -- normative intent is often written without keywords
